issues.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

- Related issue / agreed discussion, or why this is a purely mechanical documentation correction: no issue; scope is being discussed in this PR with @tt-a1i.
- Actual problem on the current base, intended outcome, and why it is worth maintaining: changes to `package.json` / `package-lock.json` (root and `archify/`) have no automated check for known advisories, new install scripts, same-version tarball/integrity swaps or `overrides` changes. This adds a non-blocking check (`mode: warn`, `fail-on-error: false`) that only runs when those files change. Example: `archify/package-lock.json` on `dev` resolves `fast-uri` 3.1.7, which is affected by GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj (fixed in 3.1.8).
- Before/after evidence entry point: reproducible examples (real #347 diff, an ordinary bump, a synthetic tarball swap) are in the PR conversation.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation and writing assistance
- Tools and model (if known), and assisted areas: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5): reviewing the existing CI, writing the workflow, running the example scans, drafting this description and replies
- Accountable contributor: @salemalem
- Problem origin: proposed improvement; the fast-uri finding came from running the scan on #347
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

Disclosure: I maintain npmscan and npmscan-action.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: CI only. Adds `.github/workflows/npmscan.yml`; no existing workflow, script or package file changes.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: never fails CI (`mode: warn`, `fail-on-error: false`). Runs only on the listed paths. Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs. On fork PRs the token is read-only, so findings go to annotations and the job summary.

## Tests run

- Base `dev` @ `8b462f6`, head `fee765a`.
- `node --test test/workflow-action-pinning.test.mjs`: 2 pass (run locally by the Agent).
- npmscan-action `scan.sh` at `de14168` run locally against the live npmscan API on the three examples in the conversation (run by the Agent).
- Not run locally: `actionlint`, full regression. Required remote CI still applies.

issues.title: Add an Atlas view to Code Analysis
issues.body:
<!-- Authors: follow CONTRIBUTING.md. Reviewers and Agents: follow REVIEWING.md. -->

## Problem and value

- Related issue / agreed discussion: none yet. Opened as a **draft** to discuss scope with a working implementation; per CONTRIBUTING.md this needs maintainer agreement before final review.
- Actual problem on the current base (`25b767c`): the Classic view reads a run against the authored architecture diagram, so its unit is the component. On a repository the author has not drawn yet, or one with many modules, the overall shape is hard to see: which modules are tangled, where complexity concentrates, where a cycle actually runs. On MyBatis 3 the overview lists 41 findings, but nothing shows that 18 of 21 modules sit in one cycle or that `executor` and `session` take part in more cross-module dependencies than any other module (270 and 212 of 749).
- Intended outcome: a second view, **Atlas**, that draws the analyzed tree itself at file and function level so problems are visible at a glance, while the Classic view stays the place to read source evidence. The Atlas links every finding back to it.
- Before/after evidence entry point: [Visual evidence](#visual-evidence) (MyBatis 3 and Apache Dubbo screenshots, how to read the Atlas, motion recording) and Tests run below. The base has no Atlas, so there is no before image; the Classic view is unchanged.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, documentation and this description.
- Tools and model: Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 — payload builder, canvas view, Classic hand-off, served-page loading, tests, docs.
- Accountable contributor: @yijiez666-alt
- Problem origin: proposed improvement.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact

- Impact class: shared behavior (overlay page) plus a new view; no schema or rule change.
  - New `overlay/atlas.mjs`: `buildAtlas({ graph, facts, findings, review })` projects the run's raw facts, module graph and findings into compact arrays (files grouped by module, one entry per resolved file-to-file dependency, every measured function with its finding, each finding with the indices it selects). `ATLAS_CSS` / `ATLAS_JS` draw it on a `<canvas>`: module arcs, file ticks, bundled dependency curves, function spikes scaled to complexity, selected findings drawn on top, polar hit testing, theme-aware colours. Motion shows change only: a reveal from the centre on opening, a cross-fade on a new focus or finding, and a light travelling around a selected import cycle in import direction; off with `prefers-reduced-motion`. The graph is painted once into an off-screen frame and composited with the motion layer and the hover mark.
  - `overlay/inject.mjs`: embeds `#bauify-atlas-data` before the Classic script (which then offers an **Atlas** button in the reader) and the Atlas style/script after it; exposes `window.__archifyShowFinding(id)` so the Atlas opens a finding with its evidence in the Classic view.
  - `bin/serve.mjs`: the served page copies the Atlas parts when present, in document order; the three Classic parts remain required.
- Preserved: Classic view behavior, payload and wording are unchanged apart from the Atlas button; without raw facts no Atlas is embedded or offered. The Atlas adds no analysis and makes no claim the findings do not: unresolved dependency records draw no curve and the side panel states their count.
- Cost: the page embeds about 1.8 MB more for Apache Dubbo (2,427 files, 13,447 dependencies, 19,439 functions) next to the existing 15.9 MB payload; a full draw takes ~40 ms on MyBatis 3 and ~110 ms on Dubbo in headless Chrome.
- PR improvement check: test-value applied below. simplify-codebase: the Atlas reuses the Classic finding page for evidence instead of a second source viewer; finding titles are computed once in the payload.
- Open questions for scope: whether the Atlas belongs in this module branch now; whether a function call graph (not extracted today, so no function-to-function curves) should follow.

## Tests run

Base `25b767c` (`labs/code-analysis`), head `f0be206`. Agent-run, Linux, Node 22.23.4, Chrome.

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| `node --test archify/modules/code-analysis/test/*.test.mjs` | 220/220 passed |
| `node --test test/core-smoke.test.mjs` | 19/19 passed |
| `ARCHIFY_CHROME=… node --test test/code-analysis*.test.mjs` | 11/11 passed |
| `node scripts/package-smoke.mjs <extracted zip>/archify` | passed (linux) |
| Manual: served view on MyBatis 3 (`0437d36`) and Apache Dubbo (shallow clone of default branch), light and dark theme | no page errors; Atlas → Classic evidence round trip works |

New tests (test-value):

- `test/atlas.test.mjs` (py-tasks fixture): every resolved in-tree file dependency drawn exactly once between the right files; files contiguous per module; every measured function kept with its measurements and reported ones pointing at their finding and back; import cycle path/files, module cycle modules and boundary imports map to the files and modules they name; a hub selects its module; accepted findings marked; no Atlas without raw facts; coverage counts every record once; unique shortest module labels; injection order. Discrimination checked by fault injection (reverted): dropping intra-module dependencies and breaking the function-to-finding link each fail their test.
- `test/code-analysis-browser.test.mjs`: opens the Atlas from the served page, checks it drew every dependency and painted the canvas, focuses a module from the side panel, selects a complex function, opens its evidence in the Classic view (source excerpt present), and checks that turning Code Analysis off closes the Atlas. It also checks motion: the opening reveal runs and finishes, a selected import cycle keeps changing the canvas, and with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` there is no cross-fade and nothing moves. Run 8 times in a row after fixing a frame-timestamp race found by this test (a requestAnimationFrame timestamp earlier than the start time sent the cycle light to index -1); all passed.

Not run: root `test:full`, Windows/macOS, Firefox/Safari, perceptual review by a human, phone-width layout beyond the CSS breakpoint. CI on this head pending at the time of writing.

## Visual evidence

Agent-captured in headless Chrome (1440×900, dark theme) on head `f0be206`, from the served view of two real repositories analyzed with `--language java`: MyBatis 3 at `0437d36` and Apache Dubbo at `843b98b` (shallow clone of the default branch). The diagram IR is a one-component placeholder, so the page title is only a label. Images are hosted on the `claude/code-atlas-evidence` branch (no product files; delete it once this PR is closed).

### How to read the Atlas

| On the circle | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Outer coloured arc | One module of the module graph; a thicker arc is a reported hub | `module-graph.json`, `coupling/hub` |
| Tick just inside an arc | One analyzed file of that module (test and generated files left out) | raw facts `files`, module graph `fileModules` |
| Curve inside the circle | One resolved dependency between two analyzed files, coloured by the importing module and bundled through both modules; hugging the rim = inside one module | raw facts `imports` (resolved, file to file) |
| Spike outside a tick | One measured function; length = cyclomatic complexity (capped at 26) | raw facts `functions` |
| Dot on a spike | A reported complex function, in its severity colour (amber warning, blue info) | `complexity/function` |
| Thick glowing curve | The selected finding: an import cycle's path, a boundary's crossing imports | `coupling/import-cycle`, `architecture/boundary` |
| Side panel | Selection, totals, findings by rule, complexity histogram, modules by coupling, dependency-record coverage, legend | same run |

Unresolved dependency records draw no curve, so a missing curve is not proof that there is no dependency; the side panel states how many there are (MyBatis: 14,652 resolved, 4,361 external, 456 unresolved of 19,469 records).

### MyBatis 3: whole repository

![Atlas overview of MyBatis 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-overview.png)

394 files in 21 modules, 1,337 file dependencies, 2,585 functions, 41 findings. Long spikes with dots mark the 27 reported complex functions; thick arcs mark the 7 hubs (`session`, `builder`, `executor`, `mapping`, `reflection`, `binding`, `type`).

### Focusing a module: `executor`

![executor focused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-focus-executor.png)

`executor` (55 files, 340 functions, fan-in 8, fan-out 12): pink curves are dependencies inside it and its 217 dependencies on other modules; light curves are the 53 dependencies of other modules on it. Everything else fades.

### Selecting a complex function

![DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-function.png)

`DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters(PreparedStatement)` in `scripting` (complexity 25, nesting 10, 93 lines, warning): its spike is ringed and the curves are its file's dependencies.

### Selecting an import cycle

![Import cycle selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-cycle.png)

A 6-file `logging` cycle drawn over the rest (path `LogFactory → Log4j2Impl → Log4j2AbstractLoggerImpl → back`). In the live page a light travels along it in import direction.

### Hand-off to the Classic view

![Classic view with source evidence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/mybatis-classic.png)

**Open evidence in Classic view** closes the Atlas and opens the same finding with its captured source excerpt and AI task; the Atlas itself shows no source.

### Apache Dubbo: scale

![Atlas overview of Apache Dubbo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/dubbo-overview.png)

2,427 files in 81 modules, 13,447 file dependencies, 19,439 functions, 258 findings. Curve opacity scales down with the number of curves so strands stay readable; long module names are cut on the circle and shown whole on hover and in the side panel.

![dubbo-common focused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/dubbo-focus-common.png)

`dubbo-common` (457 files, 5,077 functions, fan-in 73, fan-out 0): no dependencies leave it, and the light curves are the 4,705 dependencies of other modules on it — the base layer of the codebase, visible at a glance.

### Motion

![Atlas motion on MyBatis 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/47fa7a52a018768d314166ec83d310fd7af002ad/pr-1103/atlas-motion.gif)

Recorded at about 11 frames per second from CDP screenshots, so slower and choppier than the live page: the reveal on opening, the cross-fade to a focused module, and the light running around a selected import cycle. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` all three are off (covered by the browser test).

- Automated or browser checks: the browser test in Tests run (canvas painted, focus and selection state, motion and reduced motion, hand-off).
- Perceptual visual review: not performed by a human; the screenshots above are agent-captured.

## Generated artifacts

- `archify.zip`: rebuilt with `scripts/build-zip.sh` on Node 22.23.4 / zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`; package smoke passed on the extracted archive.

issues.title: fix(workflow): reserve heading clearance for inferred straight ports
issues.body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #565.

The current dev compiler rejects an ordinary same-column straight route across two lanes when its inferred top endpoint runs through a lane heading. Adding the redundant `toSide: "top"` (or `fromSide` for an upward edge) makes the same input work: the layout prepass reserved heading clearance only for explicitly authored top ports.

Reserve that same existing clearance for the forced facing ports of unpinned, same-column straight routes. This fixes layout planning at its owner instead of relaxing the collision gate or adding an authoring workaround.

## Stability impact

- Shared workflow-v2 compiler layout; deliberately limited to `route: "straight"`, distinct lanes, same column, compatible direction constraints, and diagrams without absolute coordinate pins.
- Explicit sides, absolute `via`/`channelX`/`channelY`/`labelAt` pins, collision checks, schema, and already-clear layouts are preserved. No generic routing-policy change.
- 17 existing workflow inputs in two quality profiles produce identical SVG/receipts/diagnostics versus dev (34 comparisons; 32 successful renders and two identical pre-existing `release-luna` rejections).
- Independent from the sequence heading issue #564; no dependency or merge order.

## Tests run

Comparison base: dev `629155a47cd5b487cb5a6e322b2ca71998698aaf`. Native Windows, Node 22.22.3.

- New `workflow-inferred-header-clearance.test.mjs`: baseline **7 pass / 10 fail**, candidate **17/17 pass**. Covers both directions/profiles, omitted and partially specified sides, exact explicit-port geometry, public CLI, labeled routes, pins, conflicting directions, and unchanged clear layouts.
- Nine focused workflow suites: **183/183 pass**, no skips.
- `node archify/test/golden.mjs`: **29/29 pass**; `git diff --check`: pass.
- One structured code review: no actionable findings. This is separate from executed tests.
- Complete local `npm test` finished: **2,399 tests; 2,142 pass, 56 fail, 49 cancelled, 152 skip**. This is **not green**. Matched baseline reruns reproduce **51 failures and all 49 cancellations** on unmodified dev: Windows namespaced/short-path assumptions, unavailable symlink privileges, `os.devNull`/Git fixtures, subprocess PATH dependencies, and notifier fixtures. Five PATH-dependent cases pass with the existing Git tools on the process-local PATH. **Five additional visual-check filesystem/cleanup assertions are not independently baseline-confirmed** (a selected baseline control passed), so they remain unresolved local-suite evidence, not claimed pre-existing or fixed. No global setting, unrelated product code, or assertion was changed. Complete required CI results must finish before merge.
- Exact extracted candidate ZIP: Windows package smoke passes without installing dependencies; the issue input passes all **9/9 public validation checks** with zero errors/warnings. The identical input fails on the exact baseline package.
- Actual POSIX extraction/direct CLI execution was not available locally. On the submitted head, official CI has since passed package smoke on **Ubuntu, macOS and Windows**, as well as ZIP freshness. The complete Node 18/20/22/24 test matrix is still pending at this snapshot.

## Visual evidence

- Reproduce using the minimal JSON in #565, unchanged, with `node archify/bin/archify.mjs finalize workflow INPUT OUTPUT.html --quality showcase --json`, then `visual-check OUTPUT.html --summary --require-provenance`.
- Baseline rejects the route; candidate finalizes with every gate passing. The inferred route and the explicit-side control have the same geometry: straight at x=124.2 instead of colliding with the lane heading at x=94.
- Automated evidence: all four visual-check captures pass (1440x900 and 2048x1320, light/dark).
- Perceptual review: passed for the 1440x900 light and 2048x1320 dark captures, same input/showcase/initial page. The straight A-to-B connector clears the lane heading; node/title geometry remains readable.

## Generated artifacts

- Rebuilt `archify.zip` using the unchanged canonical builder. SHA-256: `1711180f4e288b9faa91ae2c9dd62c49145fdf68f810458e7b3afd1cfc0c1eae` (2,132,601 bytes, 93 entries).
- Only the workflow compiler payload differs from the baseline archive; member list and modes are unchanged, CLI mode remains `100755`.
- Canonical baseline rebuild exactly matches the committed dev ZIP. Existing example/golden artifacts remain byte-identical, so none were churned.


## Consolidated contribution

#658 independently proposed inferred lane-header clearance and added coverage for both upward and downward omitted-side straight routes. Thanks to @Totopo27 for that contribution. The continuing regression suite here already covers both directions, omitted and partially explicit sides, plus the broader absolute-pin protections. Following the recorded maintainer decision, #567 is the continuing PR and #658 is being closed as a duplicate. This does not claim that #565 is fixed in dev or released; current-dev integration and final verification of #567 are still required.

issues.title: fix(qa): finish bounded keyboard traversal across native scroll stops
issues.body:
## Problem and behavior

A page with native scroll regions or dynamic SourceCard links can require more key presses than its initial control count. The current QA cutoff stops early and reports reachable footer controls as missing. This change freezes the initial target identities and continues real Tab/radio-arrow traversal until all initial targets are reached, a supported no-progress cycle is detected, or bounded work is exhausted.

The existing research branch is refreshed onto dev `500d4a65211ffe607fde6b3ce7505027b45bb59e`, retaining its SVG-block extraction fixes. Only the keyboard checker, its focused regressions, the canonical ZIP and experiment evidence differ from dev. Reader HTML, layout and focus order are unchanged. Scope comes from the maintainer's [ongoing research task and actual-artifact validation](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/4671df2c578925f4c70a7ec7abd68ada93a0d472/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/keyboard-current-artifacts.md).

## Boundaries and cost

Success still requires real keyboard arrival at every initial target. Hiding/removing a target or cloning its QA key cannot make it pass. Real traps and exhausted budgets remain failures. Work is bounded by initial target count + min(initial DOM elements, 1024) + 3 actions; this cost belongs to browser QA, with no new Reader dependency. The cycle check is a conservative heuristic, not a universal accessibility proof.

Scoped test-value review retained decisive scroller/SourceCard positives and identity/trap/budget negatives. No new generic focus model or frame/shadow recursion was added. Generation benchmarks do not apply: this change checks fixed HTML and does not change diagram generation.

## Verification

[Current-base reproduction and selected evidence](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/f9fc38cbc19f5bb2725fd54d957e182831eb1eb9/experiments/keyboard-traversal/refresh-dev-500d) use official Node 22.23.2 and its canonical bundled zlib:

- At tested merge `48eaf689`, render-output checks plus the Explainer caller tests: 96 passed, zero failed/skipped. Core smoke: 19 passed, zero failed/skipped. Final `f9fc38cb` adds evidence only.
- Two canonical ZIP builds and the committed ZIP are byte-identical (`712de2a5db70e88ba6cbab82b2810978da6ac4afc74ac61eecf2471499de4cf9`). All 235 entry names match current dev; only the keyboard checker entry differs. Both packed checkers equal combined source.
- Independent review verified ancestry, unchanged candidate behavior, actual logs, all recorded raw-file hashes and ZIP entries. The only base-sync conflict was the generated ZIP, rebuilt from combined source.

[Earlier browser and CLI evidence](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/tree/9601c9b6e4b6addc2f348677d1c198bc6bc74192/experiments/keyboard-traversal/refresh-dev-e837) retains tested merge `49413625`: the full real-Chrome Explainer browser file passed 19/19; public CLI browser-check on the authentic-provenance Trace HTML reached 27/27 in 33 actions across four arms, with unchanged HTML; extracted-package native scroller passed and true trap failed. These paths, the browser orchestrator, wrapper, renderer, dependencies and build script are unchanged by the latest base update. The changed static checker and its Explainer caller have the new local coverage above. This is reused evidence, not a fresh browser run.

Earlier direct-API checks on Task/Trace/OCI retain their original revision: 40/40, 27/27, 29/29 across four arms. Historical baseline 16/12/16 diagnostics remain recorded. Raw logs remain local; committed summaries include hashes and disclosed gaps, including no pre-run hash of the original delivery receipt.

Hosted CI for final head `f9fc38cbc19f5bb2725fd54d957e182831eb1eb9` is complete: 19 checks succeeded and two deployment jobs were skipped ([run 40431526745](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40431526745), attempt 2). Attempt 1 failed on the shared 1396×480 compact Sequence case; the WebM aggregate reflected browser failure while decoding succeeded. After the workflow completed, only the failed browser job was requested for rerun and its dependent aggregate followed; other successes retain attempt-1 execution. The [original failure and source-level diagnosis](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/255828331107d1c794f03a74e0695c425182c477/docs/research/2026-10-26/audit/keyboard-current-ci-diagnosis.md) remain recorded. Matching earlier #1121 geometry and a passing rerun do not establish root cause or a repaired layout defect. The previous head `9601c9b6` completed 19 checks with two deployment skips ([historical run](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/40427641788)); those results are not relabeled as this head's CI. No human acceptance, AT support, all dynamic-control coverage or reading-speed claim.

## Actual image

This existing Trace observation shows real Tab reaching the footer on the same frozen HTML. It is reused at its original identity, not a visual redesign or a new screenshot from the refreshed checker. [Capture binding and original observation](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/blob/9f9f9dacf58832f1c8784a1a24f6e04c456a4881/experiments/trace-flow-evidence/root-review/README.json).

![Actual Tab reaches the footer on unchanged HTML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tt-a1i/archify/9f9f9dacf58832f1c8784a1a24f6e04c456a4881/experiments/trace-flow-evidence/root-review/footer-tab.png)

## AI assistance and accountability

Codex/GPT-6.1-Sol reviewed the algorithm, scope and evidence; GPT-6.1-Terra refreshed the isolated tree and ran scoped checks. Accountable maintainer: @tt-a1i. Existing attribution and license notices are preserved.

- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them.

Draft for review only; no merge, release, deployment or live installation.

issues.title: feat(viewer): add GIF motion export alongside WebM
issues.body:
feat(viewer): add GIF motion export alongside WebM

Trace animations could only be exported as WebM, which requires browser
MediaRecorder support and produces a file many chat apps and doc
platforms will not preview inline. This adds GIF as a second motion
export target.

The per-frame capture setup is lifted out of recordWebm() into a shared
prepareMotionSession() that builds the static SVG background and the
authored edge/node signal scene once and hands back a draw(elapsed)
callback, so WebM and GIF sample the exact same scene and cannot drift
visually. Capability gating is split into motionTraceAvailable() (needs
only a trace animation) and canRecordMotion() (additionally needs
MediaRecorder), so GIF stays available in browsers that cannot write
WebM; unsupported menu entries degrade to a disabled tooltip.

recordGif() is a dependency-free GIF89a encoder: a 256-entry global
color table generated from a 6-7-6 uniform quantizer, then LZW
compression ported from gifenc's MIT-licensed encoder. No ffmpeg, no
npm, no Puppeteer.

Regenerates the checked-in example renders in both examples/ and
archify/examples/ plus examples/web-app.html so the golden suite stays
in sync.

Fixes #731

Closes #731

issues.body:
## Problem and value
A trailing --root causes community and release-identity checks to validate the current working directory and report success, instead of failing for the missing selected input. Stable-manifest checks throw a generic path TypeError or consume the following flag. Reject missing option values before filesystem checks.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, and description writing.
- Tools and model: Codex (model `gpt-6.1-sol`) investigated the source, wrote the change and its tests, ran the checks reported below, and drafted this description.
- Accountable contributor: @rudycelekli
- Problem origin: code inspection; a reproducible defect found by reading the current source, not an observed production or Agent failure.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

## Stability impact
Repository checker CLI inputs only; valid paths and omitted optional root defaults remain supported. All three callers share one small value reader. Focused simplify-codebase review consolidates the duplicated root handling; test-value review covers real checker subprocess outcomes and reuses their existing contracts.

## Tests run
Base 0b8f9f341760662bad37a6ff4716877220a8dedc incorrectly passes two missing-root checks and reports an unrelated TypeError in the third. Candidate passes 30/30 tests across new option-value regressions and existing registry, release identity and stable manifest contracts.

The website community build fixture includes the shared checker-options dependency in its tracked-file allowlist. The actual community-build regression reproduced the unresolved import before this follow-up and passes after it (including rejected registry entries and successful localized site publication).

issues.title: fix(workflow): make phase ownership visible without hover (#81)
issues.body:
## Problem
Phase membership was only discoverable via hover. On static first read
and in exported images, nodes near phase boundaries were visually
ambiguous. Closes #81.

## Solution
Added `renderPhaseBand()` in `render-workflow.mjs`. Renders a
full-height, low-opacity column band for each phase spanning all
swimlane rows — drawn after lane rects, before nodes/groups in SVG
paint order.

- fill-opacity 0.055 + dashed border: restrained, doesn't compete with nodes
- Colors use existing variant CSS vars (--backend-stroke, --security-stroke,
  --messagebus-stroke) — correct in all themes automatically
- Pure SVG geometry: export-safe, no JS dependency
- Phase top-rail label preserved unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- Reader can assign each node to its phase without hovering ✅
- Cue legible in both themes and exports ✅
- No duplicate phase text inside nodes ✅
- Existing workflow JSON remains valid ✅

## Changed files
- archify/renderers/workflow/render-workflow.mjs
- archify/examples/workflow-agent-tool-call-rendered.html (golden re-render)
- examples/workflow-agent-tool-call-rendered.html (golden re-render)

All golden tests pass: node test/golden.mjs → all checks passed

issues.body:

issues.title: fix: detect coincident routes in anti-parallel connections with labelAt
issues.body:
## Problem and value

Fixes #248.

Architecture connections can emit identical visible routes, especially for a bidirectional pair. Coincident geometry is not inherently invalid: a shared line can be intentional when labels clearly identify each direction. The problem is possible reader ambiguity, so showcase should warn and preserve author intent rather than reject every shared line.

## Scope

- Detect measured coincident architecture routes at showcase quality, including reversed and same-direction pairs.
- Normalize duplicate and forward-collinear route points before comparison.
- Resolve the effective CLI quality profile and skip connections with unknown endpoints.
- Report stable `composition/coincident-routes` evidence as a warning in the final artifact composition receipt.
- Keep standard quality unchanged and keep hard composition errors blocking delivery.
- Document warning-first authoring guidance; explicit `via`, `channelX`/`channelY`, or endpoint sides remain available when a warning identifies real ambiguity.
- Preserve the validated explicit-via repair and the `labelAt` removal regressions.

## Compatibility and impact

- Showcase delivery succeeds when coincident-route findings are the only composition findings; the receipt reports the warning for author review.
- Actual label clearance, crossing, containment, route rhythm, and other hard composition failures remain blocking.
- No schema change or new dependency.

## Verification

- Focused regression and artifact-check tests: `node --test archify/test/coincident-routes.test.mjs archify/test/render-output-checks.test.mjs` — 55 passed, 0 failed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `archify.zip` rebuilt with Node `22.12.0`; repeated deterministic builds match.
- Final ZIP SHA-256: `1CBA7F9ABF4D9A0FF65D51B93F07CD7A093948649717E3C109FB05671FD554CA`.
- The broader local suite was run on Windows; remaining failures are environment-dependent symlink, WSL, and Git fixture failures and are not reported as green.

## Generated artifact

`archify.zip` is regenerated from the final tracked source and included in this PR.

## Review note

The final acceptance criterion is warning-first: require all 9 artifact checks and 0 composition errors; review and report warnings, rejecting or repairing only warnings that represent actual ambiguity.

issues.title: fix(output): require explicit replacement for unrelated HTML
issues.body:
## Problem and value

Proposed implementation for #680. Current `dev` lets `render` and `deliver` replace an unrelated existing HTML file selected by `meta.output`, returning success. This draft supplies a working, tested proposal for the replacement policy before finalizing the compatibility contract.

### Proposed recognition and consent rule

- A positional CLI output path is explicit replacement intent. No new flag or interactive prompt is needed.
- Implicit output can create a new file or regenerate an existing document with recognized Archify generator metadata, primary SVG accessibility markup, and the same diagram title. Node/relationship/style edits remain convenient.
- Otherwise fail with `output/replacement-required` and suggest a new path or an explicit output argument. Refusal preserves the existing HTML; initial delivery refusal creates no provenance/journal/lock side effects.
- Apply the shared guard to direct renderers, `render`, `deliver` and `preview`, including their existing pre-publication path rechecks. Preview reuses the title it last successfully published so edits within one session keep working, and refuses unrelated content placed at its output between generations.

**Decision requested before promoting this draft:** is generator + primary-SVG markup + same title an acceptable regeneration heuristic, and is the existing positional CLI output sufficient replacement consent? This does not prove source-file identity: distinct Archify inputs with the same title can match. Renaming a diagram between invocations, unrecognized legacy/custom templates, or files above a 64 MiB recognition budget require explicit output selection. If stronger source identity is wanted, that needs a separate agreed representation rather than silently adding machine-dependent paths or new sidecars to every artifact.

## Stability impact

- Impact: shared behavior and output-acceptance contract change. Existing schema-v1 validation is unchanged, including required `meta.output`; the shared resolver's default branch is guarded where supported, without making missing authored output valid.
- Existing explicit-output, extension, input-alias, hard-link, target-change, atomic publication and delivery ownership controls remain active. The policy does not sandbox explicit CLI directories.
- Recognition is conservative and ignores marker text in comments/scripts. It is a prevention mechanism for accidental replacement, not authentication or protection against deliberately imitated Archify markup.
- No renderer geometry, HTML template, schema, version or generated example changes. Output HTML bytes stay identical; no new ownership metadata or sidecar is emitted.

## Tests run

Base: `68b77b73eaf12297356d122968d9b7b8767be278` (`dev`). Candidate: `6803a71d5c3aaf26dcd69ee7f7fb36ce60a4dbd2`.

Revision from `220b187`: removed the locale-catalog import from the standalone path-safety runtime after CI exposed missing dependencies in minimal delivery/compare and archive-build fixtures. HTML escaping remains equivalent, with quoted titles now included in the behavioral fixture. Rebuilt the ZIP. The 21 behavioral tests pass again both in the checkout and extracted ZIP; the previously failing standalone archive/unmerged-index gate also passes locally. Wider compatibility/golden evidence below was collected on `220b187`; those tests have not been relabeled as new-head results. Final-head remote CI passed; links and coverage follow.

- Reproduced silent replacement by both public `render` and `deliver` against unchanged output-related code from the base, using synthetic HTML in a temporary directory. Added failing regressions before implementation.
- `node --test test/implicit-output-replacement.test.mjs`: **21 passed**, zero failures/skips, official Node 22.23.2. Covers all ten diagram types' byte-identical regeneration, refusal/explicit replacement, different titles, metadata preservation, escaped titles, disguised marker text, default resolver selection, preview startup, live title edits and an unrelated file placed between preview generations.
- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/implicit-output-replacement.test.mjs test/meta-output-contract.test.mjs test/renderer-atomic-write.test.mjs test/preview-contract.test.mjs test/native-output-path.test.mjs`: **68 passed, 12 platform skips, 2 failed** before adding the ten-mode cases. Both failures occur while setting up Windows symlinks (`EPERM`) and reproduce using the unchanged base package/test.
- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/output-path.test.mjs test/preview.test.mjs`: **47 passed, 10 platform skips, 14 failed**. The unchanged base package reproduces 12 symlink-setup `EPERM` failures (49 passed, 10 skips). The other two were null child-process statuses; both passed in a focused rerun without code changes. These local environment/transient limitations are not claimed as a green full suite.
- `node test/golden.mjs`: all maintained output/schema checks passed.
- Generated-validator, Viewer, brand-catalogue and release-identity freshness checks, plus `git diff --check`: passed.
- Extracted ZIP outside the checkout without installing dependencies: `node scripts/package-smoke.mjs <extracted>/archify` passed, and all 21 replacement/preview/diagram-mode behavior regressions passed on `6803a71`.

Full local `npm test` and manual browser/perceptual review were not run. Final-head [CI](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37340095719) passed on `6803a71d5c3aaf26dcd69ee7f7fb36ce60a4dbd2`: full Node 18/20/22/24 test lanes, Windows Node 22/24 path contracts, three-platform package smoke, ZIP freshness, update-manifest checks, real WebM decoding and shared browser regression gate. [DSH package and distribution acceptance](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/actions/runs/37340095741) also passed on that head. Unrelated website/adapter-release jobs were skipped by workflow conditions. Local Windows limitations above remain explicit. CodeRabbit skips automatic draft review; its green status is not a completed code review.

## Generated artifacts

- Rebuilt `archify.zip` using official Node 22.23.2 / bundled zlib `1.3.1-e00f703`. SHA-256: `e355343fdd23b4c9cbae3e71629061a1ab19449806708c7afe07a8ecb27b0baa`.
- ZIP entry list is identical to the base. Only the four changed runtime modules and `references/delivery-contract.md` differ inside it. Tests remain outside the installable Skill.
- No Gallery rebuild: template/example inputs are unchanged and golden outputs pass unchanged.

issues.body:
## Problem and value

This adds a listing for [archify-index](https://github.com/Thakay/archify-index), a small standalone tool I wrote after documenting an agent integration with four Archify diagrams and opening each one from a file picker. It writes a single `index.html` beside the delivered pages and shows them in one window, one tab per diagram, opening every diagram in the same theme through the existing `?theme=` parameter. Given JSON specs, it runs `archify deliver` on them first.

It follows the package model in #663: it lives in its own repository, reads delivered pages as text and never changes them, runs no code inside Archify, and has no telemetry, hosted service or runtime dependency. It is separate from the drilldown links in #281: the index lists a set, while #281 links a node to another diagram.

## Stability impact

- Impact class and changed behavior/shared callers: metadata only. Adds `community/packages/archify-index.json`. No Archify runtime, schema, Viewer, website source or generated output changes; the catalog card is derived from the file at build time.
- Existing behavior preserved / intended compatibility changes / failure behavior: nothing in Archify changes. Three fields deserve a note.
  - `type: "wrapper"` is the closest of the five types. The tool calls the Archify CLI when it is given specs, but its main use reads pages Archify already delivered, and it never authors JSON IR. I'm happy to change the type if you read it differently.
  - `schemaVersions: [1, 2]` are the `schema_version` values of the specs it was tested with through `archify deliver`: three v1 and two v2 examples from Archify 3.0.1. The tool does not read `schema_version` itself.
  - `archify: "3.0.1"` is the only release it has been tested against. On current `dev` it labels pages of the newer diagram types from their delivery receipt or their English or Chinese description; I'll widen the range only after testing the next release.
- The name follows the existing `archify-` entries. If you would rather keep that prefix for official packages, I'll rename it.

## Tests run

- Comparison base: `dev` at 744d8e1. Candidate head: 3d84339.
- `node scripts/check-community-packages.mjs`: `community registry: 3 package(s) OK (archify-dsh, archify-hermes, archify-index).`

issues.title: chore: add scoped PR review and ZIP integration tools
issues.body:
## Problem and value

Maintainer-approved follow-up to five findings from the PR review retrospective: readiness gaps were discovered after deep review, visual proposals lacked an original control, benchmark evidence types were blurred, ZIP-only conflicts needed repeated manual integration, and scans reread unchanged PRs.

- Put scope, contributor confirmation, and applicable evidence before deep review or delegation; consolidate missing items into one author response.
- Establish the original visual defect and compare the proposal with the smallest fix on identical inputs.
- Record generation/replay/Viewer/narrower-scope evidence explicitly, preserving the existing three-PR benchmark pilot.
- Add a `gh` REST delta scanner with task-local raw evidence and a feedback-link ledger. Comments/reviews use `gh --body-file`; the helper performs no public writes or readiness decisions.
- Add an opt-in, pinned ZIP-only integration helper. It checks a clean linked worktree, refuses source conflicts, reuses the canonical builder, verifies combined source, and leaves an uncommitted merge for inspection.

Usage and stop conditions are in REVIEWING.md; the review Skill points to that single authority.

## AI assistance and accountability

- AI use: implementation, investigation, tests, documentation, and review assistance.
- Tools/models: Codex; GPT-6.1 Sol subagents implemented and independently reviewed the helpers.
- Accountable contributor: @tt-a1i
- Problem origin: observed maintainer review/integration workflow and explicit approval of the five improvements.
- [ ] I reviewed the submitted changes and explanation, understand their impact, and can answer questions about them. Validation results and gaps are recorded below.

Personal confirmation remains pending; this PR is draft because an agent cannot supply that confirmation.

## Stability impact

Repository-local maintenance tools and review guidance only. Renderer, generation instructions, validators, distributed package, and ZIP inputs are unchanged. Generation benchmark: not applicable to this scope. No new CI gate or dependency is introduced; existing conservative scope classification and ZIP freshness checks remain authoritative.

The ZIP helper never fetches, commits, pushes, approves, or merges a GitHub PR. Build failure preserves inspection state with explicit recovery instructions. Scanner timestamps are discovery signals; final head/base/check/review status must still be refreshed independently.

## Tests run

Base: `d5d979493bba650b3995836afd379cd249f2d0dd`; candidate: `dcd4343e3140612a15280a9d5dca6cbe49bded94`.

- Official Node 22.23.3 on macOS: `npm run test:focus -- test/integrate-pr-zip.test.mjs test/pr-review-scan.test.mjs` — **19 passed, 0 skipped**.
- Real disposable Git fixtures cover combined contributions, sole ZIP conflicts, dirty/source-conflict/SHA-drift refusal, and builder failure/source-mutation detection. Fixture builders validate orchestration, not canonical archive bytes; the existing builder and final CI own archive freshness.
- Scanner fixtures cover pagination, deltas, evidence retention, failed-fetch preservation, case-insensitive repository identity, and feedback recording. Fake-gh integration cases explicitly skip Windows; no Windows execution is claimed.
- Read-only live `gh` smoke: 123 open PRs across two pages; complete evidence and delta saved; immediate second scan reported zero changes. This is scan validation, not PR acceptance.
- Independent review found a repository-name casing bug; corrected and covered by a regression.
- Local documentation links resolve; `git diff --check` passed. Required remote CI is pending.

PR improvement check: applied test-value to protect source/state preservation and observable CLI outcomes, using focused Git/gh fixtures rather than renderer suites. Existing Git merge logic, canonical packaging, and CI gates are reused; no additional framework or duplicate gate was added.
